$note: Content rubrics for the (cast) farm. Each rubric = a repeatable content format with a promise, a tone, which refs/decks fit it, and how it maps to product facts in product.json. bucket: bright | product | guide | plus new ones.

rubrics.name: Hot Takes
rubrics.promise: One opinionated line about podcasting that stops the scroll.
rubrics.tone: Loud, contrarian, editorial. No product until the last card.
rubrics.shape: photo hook → stat → statement → tags → steps → poster rule → features → splash
rubrics.example: Nobody stays for the warm-up. / Your title is why nobody clicked.

rubrics.name: Inspiration
rubrics.promise: Motivate the creator to make and ship the thing — mindset over features.
rubrics.tone: Warm, encouraging, a little defiant. Speaks to the person, not the product.
rubrics.shape: you-have-something hook → truth → the fear/excuses → reframe → quote → nudge → soft product bridge → splash
rubrics.purpose: Top-of-funnel brand affinity: meet creators who 'have something worth saying' but are stuck on production, remove the fear, and position Cast as the thing that finishes it — product only as the enabler at the end.
rubrics.example: You have something worth saying. / Done beats perfect. / Nobody starts good.
rubrics.productTie: soft — brand affinity; product appears only as the enabler on the last two cards

rubrics.name: Feature Drop
rubrics.promise: One feature, shown as the fix to one concrete pain.
rubrics.tone: Direct, confident, benefit-first. Names the feature.
rubrics.shape: pain hook → how it works (steps) → feature grid → CTA splash
rubrics.example: Censoring should be part of editing — not another job after it.
rubrics.productTie: hard — one named feature is the subject

rubrics.name: One Workflow
rubrics.promise: Show the whole record→export pipeline living in one place vs a mess of tools.
rubrics.tone: Calm, systemic. The hero is the pipeline, not a single feature.
rubrics.shape: before (tool chaos) → the six steps as a grid → after → splash
rubrics.example: Transcript → cleanup → censor → chapters → music → export. One place.

rubrics.name: Plan Picker
rubrics.promise: Which plan fits which creator — Free/Lite/Plus/Max at a glance.
rubrics.tone: Plain, honest, no hype. Always verify live pricing.
rubrics.shape: who-are-you hook → plan tiles → what-you-get → CTA
rubrics.warning: Verify pricing page before publish; prices in product.json may drift.

rubrics.name: How-To
rubrics.promise: A concrete 3-step method a creator can act on today — with or without Cast.
rubrics.tone: Helpful, specific, teacher voice. Product is the shortcut, not the gate.
rubrics.shape: problem → 3 numbered steps → rule → features → splash
rubrics.example: Move your best line to the top: find it in the transcript, cut it, paste at 0:00.

rubrics.name: Mistakes
rubrics.promise: A list of things creators get wrong, named fast, then the fix.
rubrics.tone: Blunt but useful. The tag wall is the payload.
rubrics.shape: verdict hook → stat → the-truth → tag wall of mistakes → fix steps → splash
rubrics.example: Openings die of: hellos, mic checks, the weather, housekeeping…

rubrics.name: Myth vs Fact
rubrics.promise: Kill one persistent belief about podcast production with a fact.
rubrics.tone: Corrective, credible. Leans on real product boundaries.
rubrics.shape: myth card → fact card → why → feature → splash
rubrics.example: Myth: you need a better mic. Fact: listeners hear the room, not the mic.

rubrics.name: Before / After
rubrics.promise: Raw recording vs finished episode — the transformation Cast delivers.
rubrics.tone: Satisfying, tangible. Two states, hard contrast.
rubrics.shape: before (raw, messy) → the pass → after (clean) → splash
rubrics.example: Um, uh, like → gone. Dead air → gone. Room hum → gone.

rubrics.name: Unnecessary Censorship
rubrics.promise: Comedy format — bleep ordinary words for effect, powered by custom censoring.
rubrics.tone: Playful, absurd, meme-adjacent. The joke sells the feature.
rubrics.shape: setup → over-bleeped punchline → 'yes you can do this in Cast' → splash
rubrics.example: Bleep your co-host's name every time. Bleep the word 'algorithm.'
